How To Read The Dossier
A few terms that will be helpful to understand as you read your dossier.
In psychology and storytelling, archetypes are familiar human patterns. This is particularly useful to know as you build your brand because it helps make your brand feel consistent and gives your brand a recognizable role. It helps people understand what they can expect from you and gives your voice, content, and visual choices a consistent direction.
The logo, colors, photographs, and type that make a brand recognizable. Photographs show your colors in real settings, the way people will meet them, beyond the logo, the words, and blocks of color. Used the same way every time, these elements help people recognize you quickly.
Your brand foundation is what you naturally and unconsciously communicate to the world. The clearer it is, the better your interests, instincts, and values work together to give your brand a solid base to build on.
Something you believe, based on real experience, that goes against what most people in your niche currently say. These are listed because a contrarian belief stated clearly and often is one of the fastest ways an audience remembers who you are.
Real research into what actual questions your audience is already asking. Especially the questions they’re not getting good answers to. Those gaps show you where there is room to say (or show) something useful and specific without repeating what everyone else is already saying. To stand out. An opportunity to become the authority within your niche.

Content Pillars
A content pillar is a core topic that supports everything you publish. Every blog post, video, newsletter and social media update links back to one of your pillars. Your pillars appear later in this Dossier, drawn from your questionnaire answers. They keep your message focused, and build authority around your expertise.

SEVEN RULES FOR USING THEM
1
Use two fonts only. The display font carries headlines and short statements. The body font carries everything else. Create hierarchy with size and weight.
2
Keep headlines short. One or two lines, set large enough to read at a glance.
3
Set body text at 16 pixels or larger, about 12 points in print, in your darkest color on a light background.
4
Match the text color to its background. Use the pairings shown above. They stay readable in every size.
5
Choose one accent color for each layout. Use it for one thing, such as a single word, a button, or a line.
6
Use the same pairing everywhere. Website, social posts, packaging, and documents should look related. Repetition is how people begin to recognize you.
7
Leave generous space around text. Space makes type look deliberate and easier to read.
